# runr_binding (Resource)

A binding of the organization: a managed `kv` store (Redis), `object` storage (S3), a `postgres` database, or `external` credentials. Attach it to projects with `runr_binding_attachment`; its connection details reach the functions as environment variables.

Credentials are never part of the state: the API returns them only from `runr bindings credentials` (permission `bindings.view_credentials`, audited). The `values` of an external binding are write-only: Terraform keeps what it set.

Destroying the resource deletes the binding with retention: it is detached at once and its data is kept for the retention period (`runr bindings restore` brings it back). Its name stays taken until the data is purged, so a replacement needs a new `name`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A KV store on the region's Redis: a user limited to its own key prefix.
resource "runr_binding" "cache" {
  name      = "cache"
  type      = "kv"
  region_id = data.runr_region.eu.id
  memory_mb = 128
}

# A Postgres database on the region's shared CloudNativePG cluster.
resource "runr_binding" "orders_db" {
  name              = "orders-db"
  type              = "postgres"
  region_id         = data.runr_region.eu.id
  storage_gb        = 2
  connection_limit  = 10
  statement_timeout = "15s"
}

# A dedicated Postgres cluster with a replica and daily backups.
resource "runr_binding" "reports_db" {
  name       = "reports-db"
  type       = "postgres"
  plan       = "dedicated"
  region_id  = data.runr_region.eu.id
  storage_gb = 20
  instances  = 2
  backups    = true
  timeout    = "20m"
}

# An S3 bucket with a quota and a key allowed on that bucket only.
resource "runr_binding" "files" {
  name      = "files"
  type      = "object"
  region_id = data.runr_region.eu.id
  quota_gb  = 10
}

# Credentials you bring, injected as they are (write-only).
resource "runr_binding" "payments" {
  name = "payments"
  type = "external"
  values = {
    PAYMENTS_URL   = "https://pay.example.com"
    PAYMENTS_TOKEN = var.payments_token
  }
}

variable "payments_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name (lower case letters, digits and `-`, at most 30 characters; unique in the organization).
- `type` (String) `kv`, `object`, `postgres` or `external`.

### Optional

- `backups` (Boolean) `postgres` dedicated: daily base backup and WAL archive to the region object store (default off).
- `connection_limit` (Number) `postgres`: connections of the role and the database (default 20).
- `instances` (Number) `postgres` dedicated: 1 primary plus replicas, up to 3 (default 1).
- `memory_mb` (Number) `kv`: memory the binding's keys may use (default 64); above it the user can only read and delete.
- `plan` (String) `postgres`: `shared` (default; a database on the region's shared cluster) or `dedicated` (a cluster of its own). Other types: computed.
- `quota_gb` (Number) `object`: bucket quota in GB (default 5).
- `region_id` (String) Region of a `kv`, `object` or `postgres` binding (required for those; external bindings have none). It can be attached to projects of that region.
- `statement_timeout` (String) `postgres`: `statement_timeout` of the role (default `30s`).
- `storage_gb` (Number) `postgres`: size limit (shared, default 1) or volume size per instance (dedicated, default 5; it can only grow).
- `timeout` (String) How long `wait` waits (Go duration, default `10m`); a dedicated Postgres cluster takes a few minutes.
- `values` (Map of String, Sensitive) `external`: the variables to inject (names upper case, digits and `_`). Write-only: Terraform keeps what it set; changing them updates the attached projects.
- `wait` (Boolean) Wait at create until the binding is provisioned (`ready`; default `true`).

### Read-Only

- `env_keys` (List of String) Variables an attachment injects (without its prefix).
- `id` (String) Binding id.
- `over_quota` (Boolean) The binding is over its size limit: writes are refused until data is deleted or the limit is raised.
- `resource_name` (String) Name of the binding's resources on the data service (bucket, Redis user, database).
- `status` (String) `provisioning`, `ready`, `rotating` or `error`.
- `status_message` (String) Reason of an `error` status.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <binding name or id>
terraform import runr_binding.orders_db orders-db
```
